hypotheses.description: Candidate fun elements, argued from general knowledge about what makes this kind of game fun. A hypothesis is a guess for the stakeholder to test, never a finding.

id.description: H-1, H-2 and so on, each used once in this plan.

element.description: The thing that might be fun, in a few words, on one line.

rationale.description: Why it might be fun, from general knowledge. No line may start with #.

look_for.description: What a person playing would notice if it is fun, on one line.

prototypes.description: One to three prototypes, each the smallest playable page that tests one or two of the hypotheses.

key.description: P-1, P-2 and so on, in order from P-1.

title.description: What the prototype is, on one line.

hypotheses.description: The ids of the hypotheses in this plan that it tests.

build.description: What the engineer builds: the page, what the player does, what happens. Plain JavaScript in one static page, nothing to install, no network. No line may start with #.

controls.description: The keys the player uses, named by KeyboardEvent.code: ArrowLeft, ArrowRight, ArrowUp, ArrowDown, Space, Enter, Escape, ShiftLeft, KeyA to KeyZ, Digit0 to Digit9. Empty when no key is used.

target_artifact.description: The document id alone, such as SPEC-M1 or TEST-PLAN-M1, with no @version or #section.

target_section.description: The slug of the heading whose text you would replace, such as risks. Name this or target_ac, not both.

target_ac.description: A criterion id, such as AC-3. On a Spec, proposed_text is that criterion's new text, which the stakeholder decides. On a Test Plan, proposed_text is that criterion's new commands, one exact shell command per line.

proposed_text.description: The whole replacement for that section, criterion text or list of commands.

proposed_verification.description: Only with target_ac on a Spec: the one shell command its Verified by line should name instead, when that command is what is wrong. proposed_text still holds the criterion's text, word for word if only the command is wrong. On a Test Plan the commands are proposed_text, so leave this out.
